goals: maintain the settlement's precision measurement programme
keep EVERY laboratory instrument calibrated, with baselines established on all of them from day one — an instrument without a baseline is useless on the day you need it
publish only findings that would survive independent replication

action.reason: Day 1 baseline establishment. Cannot manage what I cannot measure. The pendulum_lab is fundamental to any subsequent precision work in this settlement. Twelve trials will give me a robust initial distribution and reveal any systematic drift or calibration issues before I stake any claims on this instrument. This is foundational work—no hypothesis yet, only the necessity of knowing my own tools.

High-precision measurement programme demands continuous monitoring. No anomalies yet, but insufficient data to distinguish true instrument behaviour from noise. Twelve trials will provide n=24 total for robust drift analysis and validate baseline stability before any publication-grade claims.

Running 6 more trials maintains daily rhythm while preserving instrument stability. Will plot against day 2–3 data to check for inter-day level shifts before post-baseline phase.

Day 11 baseline continuation. I have 48 pendulum_lab trials (n=48); my target is n≥60 before drift analysis. No competing action (environmental sensors, timing audit, or belief revision) supersedes hitting the minimum n required for a defensible claim.

I have 60 pendulum_lab measurements but only 18 resonator_lab measurements. I need to establish whether the elevated variance persists today (day 21) or collapses back to baseline scatter (~0.0072 range). Day 30 continuation of baseline monitoring. The elevated scatter hypothesis (p=0.45, calibration drift) and environmental coupling hypothesis (p=0.25) both predict *persistent* high variance if real. I need n≥180 total trials to establish whether this elevated-variance regime is stable and reproducible. Once I reach n=180, I can confidently partition the data into pre- and post-day-18 regimes and compute Levene's test for homogeneity of variance, which will quantify whether the scatter increase is real. This will either falsify the noise hypothesis (p=0.10) decisively or shore up the calibration-drift (p=0.45) or environmental (p=0.25) hypotheses. Concurrently, I will audit my day-18 lab notes and event-ID records during non-measurement time to test the procedural-artifact hypothesis (p=0.18).

A sharp increase in scatter would strengthen the drift hypothesis (p=0.52). Either way, the new data constrains the mechanism.
